records.title: Rear hatch lift struts weaken and fail to hold the tailgate open
records.description: Both rear hatch gas struts on the B5 A4 Avant lose pressure over time as the internal seals dry out. Cold weather accelerates the failure. The first sign is the hatch slowly drifting downward after being opened; the second is the hatch dropping suddenly under its own weight, which can hit a person loading cargo. By 100,000 miles or 15 years almost every original-equipment strut has weakened past the point of holding the lid up. Some owners also report the strut ball mounts on the body backing out, allowing the struts to detach completely.
records.solution: Replace both struts as a pair — never one at a time, since unmatched strut pressures stress the hinges. OEM Stabilus struts from Audi or aftermarket equivalents (StrongArm, Strut Master, Hayman) cost $20-40 per pair. The job is 10-15 minutes with a flat-head screwdriver to release the spring clips on each ball end. If the body ball mounts have backed out, remove them, apply blue Loctite to the threads, and torque to ~22 N·m.
symptoms: Rear hatch drifts down slowly after being opened
Hatch drops suddenly when released, won't stay up
Hatch rebounds without latching when closing
Loose strut ball mounts rattle when door is shut
Cold-weather failure more pronounced than summer

citations.title: Avant Tailgate: Loose Strut Ball Mounts — Audizine

communityRecommendations.content: StrongArm 6526 lift supports are the most-recommended aftermarket replacement — Stabilus-equivalent quality at half the OEM price.
Always replace both struts as a pair. Mixing old and new struts stresses the hatch hinges and can crack the inner mounting points.
If the strut ball mounts on the body rattle loose, take them out, apply blue Loctite, and torque to 22 N·m. This prevents the strut from popping off entirely.

records.title: Window regulator plastic clips and cable pulley fail, window drops into door
records.description: The B5 platform uses a cable-operated window regulator with green plastic clips holding the glass to the cable car. The clips are the dedicated wear point — they crack from heat cycling and cable tension, releasing the glass which then drops into the door cavity. Less commonly, the upper pulley (also plastic) shatters when the cable jumps off, severing the cable. The issue affects all B5 A4 body styles (sedan and Avant wagon) and is well-documented across the 1996-2001 production run. Failure pattern: window rolls down fine but will not go up, or rolls up briefly then drops back down.
records.solution: Two repair paths. Path 1 (cheap, fast): replace just the broken green clips — eBay/aftermarket sets are $20-30, swap takes 30 min per door without removing the regulator. Path 2 (durable): full regulator assembly with stainless or ball-bearing pulleys ($80-150 per door from ECS Tuning, FCP Euro, IDParts). Removing the old regulator requires drilling out the pop rivets on the door shell, so a heavy-duty rivet gun and replacement stainless rivets are needed. Many owners on later B5 cars do the full regulator job because the second clip fails within a year of the first.
symptoms: Rear window won't roll up, motor still spins
Window rolls up briefly then drops back down
Glass falls into the door cavity with a thunk
Grinding or fluttering noise from inside the door when switch is pressed
Window sits crooked in the channel

citations.title: DIY: B5 A4/S4 Window Regulator Fix — Audizine
Rear Window Regulator Replacement (lengthy) — AudiWorld B5 platform

communityRecommendations.content: ECS Tuning sells complete B5 A4 window regulators with improved metal pulleys — the durable long-term fix vs replacing just the plastic clips.

Cheap option: green plastic clip sets are $20-30 on eBay. Takes 30 min per door. Skips drilling rivets but the second clip usually fails within a year, so most owners eventually do the full regulator.
Pop the door panel BEFORE buying parts — confirm whether it's the clips, the cable, or the motor. Sometimes a worn cable spool inside the motor mimics regulator failure.
Don't reuse the original aluminum pop rivets when you replace the regulator. Use stainless 4.8 mm rivets — aluminum corrodes against the steel cable car.

records.title: Bosch 5.3 ABS Control Module Internal Failure
records.description:
The problem begins with three beeps, a solid yellow ABS light and a flashing red brake light. The warning may come on momentarily while driving and go away, but in most cases will become more prevalent as time goes on. It seems to be a common problem with Audi A4 and VW Passat B5 models. These models use the Bosch 5.3 ABS system.
 
Failed Bosch 5.3 control modules are extremely common in 2000-era Audis.
 Internal bond-wire/solder-joint failures inside the controller (ultrasonically bonded substrate connections degrading in the hot engine bay) break communication with wheel-speed sensors and disable ABS/EDL.
records.solution:
A typical fault is: Control Module Part Number 8E0 614 111 M, Component/Version: ABS/EDS 5.3 QUATTRO D31, Software Coding 0273004134, Fault Found: 65535 - Internal Control Module Memory Error 35-00.
 
Audi does not sell the control unit by itself — you must purchase the entire Control Module, Pump and Valve assembly, which cost approximately $1950 for an 8E0 614 111 M.
 The economical fix is to unbolt only the electronic controller (6 Torx screws) and send it to Module Master, XeMODeX, or cheapabs.com for ~$150-350 rebuild with no recoding needed.

citations.title: BOSCH ABS Control Module Applications in Audi Vehicles - cheapabs.com
Anti-Lock Brake Module 5.3 Repair For Audi A4,A6,A8 | XeMODeX
Bosch 5.3 Audi Cadillac Ford Hyundai Maserati Pontiac Saab Volkswagen – Module Master

communityRecommendations.content: Only remove the electronic module half (6 Torx screws on the side) — leave the hydraulic block bolted to the car so you don't have to bleed the entire brake system after reinstallation.
OBD-II generic scanners will not read ABS codes on this car. You need VAG-COM/VCDS or an equivalent VAG-protocol tool to confirm the module is the failure point.

records.title: Retractable Cargo Cover Latch and Spring Failure
records.description: The retractable cargo cover latch mechanisms on either side break, preventing the cover from staying attached to the D-pillars. The internal spring that retracts the cover also weakens or breaks, leaving the cover hanging loose.
records.solution: Replace broken latch clips (available individually from Audi parts). If the retract spring is broken, the entire cargo cover cassette must be replaced. Aftermarket covers are available at lower cost than OEM.

records.title: Takata NADI Driver Airbag Inflator Recall (Audi 69AE / NHTSA 20V056)
records.description:
VW is recalling certain 2000-2001 TT Roadster, 2000 TT Coupe, 1999 Audi A8, 1998-2000 Audi A6, and 1999-2000 Audi A4 vehicles equipped with Non-Azide Driver air bag Inflators (NADI) that do not contain phase stabilized ammonium nitrate (PSAN) propellant, and due to a manufacturing issue, the NADI inflators may absorb moisture, possibly causing the air bag to deploy improperly in the event of a crash.
 
The air bag may deploy slowly during a crash, so it won't protect you as designed, or the inflator may deploy aggressively and even explode, with metal parts that could injure or kill someone.
 Note: the 1998 A4 model year is not included in the U.S. 69AE campaign — only 1999-2000 A4 sedans/wagons. (1997-1998 A4s were later addressed under a separate recall, 69BT, after being mistakenly omitted from 20V056. Later-build 2000-2002 A4/S4 vehicles were covered under recall 69CJ.)
records.solution:
VW will notify owners, and dealers will replace the driver frontal air bag inflator with an alternative inflator when the parts become available, free of charge; owner notifications were expected to begin March 27, 2020. Owners may contact Audi customer service at 1-800-253-2834. Volkswagen's number for this recall is 69AE.
 Enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to confirm open recall status; the remedy is performed free at any Audi dealer.
symptoms: potential for shrapnel injury in a crash

communityRecommendations.content: Even if the airbag light is off, the inflator can still be defective. Have the VIN checked at the dealer — the repair is free under campaign 69AE.

records.title: Panoramic Sunroof Drain Tube Clogging
records.description: The panoramic sunroof drain tubes on the A4 Avant clog with debris, causing water to overflow into the headliner, A-pillars, and footwells. Left unchecked, this damages the electronics under the carpet including the comfort control module.
records.solution: Clear all four sunroof drain tubes using compressed air or a flexible cleaning wire. Clean the sunroof channel tray. Inspect and replace any cracked drain tube connections at the roof corners.

communityRecommendations.content: Clean all four drain tubes every spring and fall — prevention is far cheaper than replacing a water-damaged comfort module

records.title: Rear Upper Shock Mount Bushing Wear
records.description: Rear upper shock mount bushings wear out, causing a knocking noise from the rear when going over bumps. The Avant's heavier rear end accelerates bushing wear compared to the sedan. Common after 60,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace rear upper shock mount bushings. Consider replacing rear shocks at the same time if over 80,000 miles. Bilstein B4 or Sachs OE replacements are recommended. Realign rear suspension after service.
